# Datadog Integration — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Datadog Integration. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The Agent MongoDB check supports custom find, count and aggregate metrics. Database Monitoring adds query snapshots, slow-query metrics, execution plans and collection insights beyond the standard integration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/README.md
- [statement] Datadog's standard MongoDB integration distinguishes Database Monitoring as an additional product for query snapshots, slow-query metrics, database load and execution plans. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/README.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Atlas provides cluster, replica-set and database tags on relevant metrics. Custom tags require opt-in and apply to metrics rather than alerts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md
- [statement] Atlas warns that mongodb.atlas.replstatus.health can remain healthy when nodes stop sending pings, or become inaccurate during partitions and Datadog ingestion problems. Configure no-data monitoring rather than treating health=1 alone as proof of availability. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md
- [statement] Atlas exposes organization, project, cluster and database tags. User-defined resource tags are optional and apply to metrics rather than alerts. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md · keywords: Datadog Integration · also: https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/mongodb-atlas/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas pushes metrics into Datadog; setup uses a Datadog API key in Atlas project integrations. Both vendors document an M10+ cluster requirement. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md · keywords: Datadog Integration · also: https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/mongodb-atlas/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-integrations-create-DATADOG.md, https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/README.md
- [statement] Atlas setup requires a Datadog API key. The CLI command atlas integrations create DATADOG creates or updates the project integration. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md · keywords: Datadog Integration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-integrations-create-DATADOG.md
- [statement] Atlas can deliver alerts as Datadog events through the same integration used for project metrics. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md · keywords: Datadog Integration · also: https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/mongodb-atlas/
- [statement] Atlas disables high-cardinality database, collection-latency and query-shape metric exports by default; enable sendDatabaseMetrics, sendCollectionLatencyMetrics and sendQueryShapeMetrics explicitly. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md · keywords: Datadog Integration · also: https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/mongodb-atlas/
- [statement] The MongoDB check ships with the Datadog Agent. Its configuration uses mongo.d/conf.yaml and a monitoring user with clusterMonitor plus read permissions for the databases being monitored. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/README.md · keywords: Datadog Integration · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-monitor-mongodb-with-datadog/view
- [statement] MongoDB APM requires instrumentation in the application making database requests. OneUptime illustrates initializing Node.js dd-trace before importing the MongoDB client; installing the database metric check alone does not establish application tracing. (high confidence) — https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/README.md · keywords: Datadog Integration · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-monitor-mongodb-with-datadog/view
- [statement] The Agent integration collects low-level metrics per mongod node, while higher-level collection/index statistics require topology-aware placement. Datadog documents separate replica-set and sharded-cluster layouts. (low confidence) — https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/README.md
- [statement] The MongoDB integration changelog records safeguards against monitoring overhead and failures: skipping explain on $mergeCursors pipelines to prevent potential crashes, and removing queryStats server-side sorting to avoid sort-memory failures. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-08) — https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/CHANGELOG.md
- [statement] A February 2023 Terraform user reported INTEGRATION_FIELDS_INVALID and INVALID_ENUM_VALUE errors while configuring Datadog region values through the Atlas API. The captured thread records differing Atlas and Terraform documentation values and no follow-up confirming a fix. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/integration-fields-invalid-error-from-atlas-api-when-trying-to-enable-datadog-integration/214371
- [statement] A Datadog-authored Chef guest post shows automated Agent deployment and configuration of the MongoDB integration through Chef roles; this remains vendor-origin evidence. (low confidence) — https://www.chef.io/blog/datadog-x-chef-how-and-why-these-two-platforms-go-together
- [statement] Atlas requires Project Owner access for this integration; an Organization Owner must first add themselves to the project with that role. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/datadog-integration.md
- [statement] Datadog recommends an Agent on each replica-set host, connecting to its local member. Low-level metrics require collection from every mongod, while higher-level collection/index statistics should be collected once. (low confidence) — https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/README.md
- [statement] MongoDB logs require a separate Agent configuration: enable logs_enabled in datadog.yaml and configure the MongoDB log source. Log collection is disabled by default. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/master/mongo/README.md
